li: Quick heads-up — after we bumped continuous_batching.token_budget_target to 0.6 on the private-vpc small-gpu pool, profiling shows a 15–30% tail latency regression for short requests (<64 tokens). KV cache hit rate down ~12% vs baseline. p95 went from ~120ms -> ~160ms on canary.

asha: ugh. do you have the profiler traces or perf-ci link? :eyes:

li: Perf trace: https://perf-ci.internal/runs/2026-03-15/patch-abc123 — key bits: more frequent kernel fallback from optimized fused-attn -> generic attention, and noticeably higher memcpy time in kv_cache eviction path.

ben: quick question — did we change microbatcher window or the prefix packing heuristic in the same rollout? token_budget_target should encourage larger batches, not more fallbacks.

li: We only changed token_budget_target and lowered conservative_queue_wait_ms from 8 -> 4 in the same pr to reduce single-request latency. Config snippet:
```
continuous_batching:
  token_budget_target: 0.6
  conservative_queue_wait_ms: 4
  allow_inflight_prefix_merge: true
```
I suspect lowering conservative wait exposes more heterogeneous sequence-length mixes into a batch which breaks kernel selection assumptions.

mike: I _think_ the kernel selector uses the batch's max_seq and avg_seq distribution to pick fused kernels. If we pack short requests with one long request, max_seq spikes and forces a fallback kernel even though avg_seq is small. That would explain p95 regressions.

asha: makes sense. KV cache thrash could be from more prefix merges happening while conservative wait is low — more inflight merges -> more evictions on small GPUs. Can you dump kv metrics?

li: KV metrics: kv_hit=0.88 -> 0.76 after change, avg_evictions/sec +22%, memcpy bytes up ~1.8x in the kernel boundary.

perf-ci: Regression introduced in commit abc123 (continuous batching heuristic patch). The CI perf diff highlights increased host->device memcpy and higher kernel launch counts.

ben: Proposed quick mitigation: revert conservative_queue_wait_ms to 8 and keep token_budget_target at 0.5 (instead of 0.6) for the private pool. Also add a microbatcher tweak: prefer packing by seq_len bucket (+/- 16 tokens) to avoid mixing very short and long sequences.

mike: Agreed. Could also add a fast-path in kernel selector: if avg_seq < 64 && max_seq/avg_seq > 3 then prefer per-seq packing or split the batch to avoid fused kernel fallback.

li: I'll run a canary with:
```yaml
continuous_batching:
  token_budget_target: 0.5
  conservative_queue_wait_ms: 8
  seq_len_bucket_width: 16
```
Deploying to small-gpu private pool now.

deploy-bot: canary deploy triggered by li at 2026-03-15T21:12Z — job id deploy-7892.

asha: once canary is up, please capture tail latency, kv_hit, memcpy-bytes and kernel-fallback-rate (per-minute) for 30m.

li: will do. initial canary numbers (first 10m): p95 ~125ms, kv_hit=0.86, memcpy-down ~30%, kernel-fallback-rate down by 60%. Looks promising.

ben: if that holds, let's push the config as a private/pool override only (do not apply to hosted). We should also add unit tests for the kernel selector threshold so future tuning doesn't regress this.

mike: opened issue #INF-1247 to add a deterministic kernel selector test that simulates mixed seq_len distributions. Assigning to eng-runtime.

li: action items: 1) finish 30m canary and post full perf trace; 2) create rollout config for private-pool override; 3) add kernel selector unit tests. I'll follow up in this thread with the trace link. :thumbsup:

perf-ci: noted. CI will run the regression check on the selector test once merged.
